starter_files.contents:
# Document Management API

## Objective
Store and manage user-owned documents safely.

## Runtime
Express 5.x on a supported Node.js LTS release. Install dependencies from the local package manifest/lockfile.

## Required behavior
- File uploads and metadata
- User/resource permissions
- Private download endpoints
- Upload restrictions and cleanup

## API contract
Document method, path, request body, authentication, response status/body, and expected errors for every endpoint.

## Verification
Test success, malformed input, not-found, unauthorized access where relevant, and one dependency failure. Record actual commands and results.

## Security and cleanup
Use only synthetic data; keep credentials in environment variables; remove temporary files/records after testing.

# Acceptance checklist

- [ ] API routes and status codes match the documented contract.
- [ ] Request schemas reject missing, malformed, oversized and unsupported values.
- [ ] Permission checks run server-side for every protected resource.
- [ ] Error responses are consistent and do not reveal stack traces or secrets.
- [ ] Automated tests cover normal, negative, boundary and dependency failure cases.
- [ ] Setup/reset commands work from a clean checkout.
- [ ] Logs, health checks and deployment smoke tests are documented.

stretch_features: Add request correlation IDs and a concise observability dashboard.
Add contract tests and a repeatable CI check.
Document a safe rollback and data-recovery procedure appropriate to the project.
acceptance_criteria: Document every route with method, path, authentication, request fields and response/error contract.
Use supported Express 5 syntax and validate all untrusted input.
Use parameterized queries and transactions where persistence or multi-step state changes are involved.
Test success, bad input, authorization failure, not-found and dependency failure as applicable.
Keep secrets server-side and provide reproducible setup, smoke-test and cleanup instructions.
test_plan: Start from a clean local checkout and follow the README commands.
Run automated tests and record their actual result.
Use an HTTP client to verify representative routes and status/body values.
Test one invalid request and one simulated dependency failure.
Review logs for secret leakage and document reset/cleanup steps.
review_method: Human review of source, API contract, actual local tests and documented evidence. CodeLeaf does not execute the starter project or provision external services.
status_note: Mapped to the attached PDF Section D. Requirements are complete at blueprint level; every project still needs an independently run implementation/review before publication.
